references.text: Moses urges the children of Israel to bring offerings for the sanctuary, which is the background for the gifts received in 36:3.
Describes how the people brought voluntary offerings for the work on the tabernacle, which is the same action that continues in 36:3.
God's first command to collect offerings (terumah) from the people for the sanctuary, fulfilled in 36:3.
The continuation of the people's generosity, where so much was given that Moses had to stop them from bringing more.
David's collection of voluntary gifts for the temple reflects the same principle of willing sacrifice for God's house.
Paul describes how the churches' generosity exceeded expectations, just as the Israelites gave more than was needed.
The principle of voluntary and cheerful giving reflects the same spirit as the morning offerings of the Israelites in the wilderness.
Both verses document the people's willing contributions during the building of the sanctuary, where 35:29 establishes the motive and 36:3 shows the result.
Complementary verses showing respectively the collection phase and the completion of the sanctuary's construction.
Both verses confirm that the work on the sanctuary was carried out exactly according to God's command, from collection to completion.
